title: Soupy Rice with Chicken, Puerto Rican Style

content.title: About
content.content: Soupy rice with chicken, Puerto Rican style is a traditional island dish featuring rice cooked in a flavorful chicken broth with pieces of chicken, tomatoes, sweet peppers, garlic, and spices such as adobo and cumin. The result is a hearty, slightly spicy and mildly sweet one‑pot meal.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The dish originated in rural Puerto Rico as a way to stretch leftover chicken with simple pantry staples.
Rice is traditionally simmered in the chicken broth, giving it a richer taste and texture.
Adobo seasoning—a blend of garlic, oregano, mustard powder, and vinegar—is a key flavor component.
It is often served with fried plantains or avocado to balance the savory heat.
Variations may replace chicken with shrimp or other seafood.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Chicken provides complete, high‑quality protein essential for muscle repair and growth.

items.title: Complex carbohydrates
items.content: Rice supplies steady‑release energy, helping maintain stable blood‑sugar levels.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The dish contains thiamine, niacin, and vitamin B6, which support metabolism and nervous‑system health.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Chicken and rice contribute iron, zinc, and magnesium, important for immunity and muscle function.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Tomatoes and sweet peppers add lycopene and vitamin C, which help combat oxidative stress.

items.title: Chicken allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to chicken, experiencing skin or digestive reactions.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Prepared adobo mixes or store‑bought broth can raise sodium levels, which may be a concern for hypertension.

items.title: Food‑borne illness risk
items.content: Chicken must be cooked to an internal temperature of 75 °C (165 °F) to eliminate salmonella.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the hot rice stew in a deep bowl. Garnish with fresh cilantro, a squeeze of lime, or fried plantains for extra flavor. It works well as a main lunch or dinner and is convenient for outdoor meals.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Cool leftovers in an airtight container and refrigerate for 3‑4 days. Reheat until boiling before serving. The dish can be frozen for up to 2 months, portioned beforehand.
